LESSON: WRITING 8.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING: SELF-ASSESSMENT

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.5: Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment, part of Strand 8 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to assess writing? 2. How can one improve their composition writing skills?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify steps involved in the assessment of narrative compositions,

   Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write narrative compositions and assess the introduction, body, and conclusion,

   Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the importance of assessment in improving narrative composition writing.

   Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online and offline for information on the aspects of self-assessment

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online and offline for information on the aspects of self-assessment

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner watches a video or listens to a recording on how to peer assess a composition.

Values:
Integrity is achieved as the learner learns to be honest and truthful while assessing the composition of peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer education is enhanced as the learner assesses the composition of peers.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the skills of assessing own composition to assessing compositions and essays in subjects such as Kiswahili.
